title: AI as a Service, in one breath
oneliner: AIaaS = prebuilt, pre-trained AI capabilities from your cloud provider - AWS AI services, IBM Watson, Azure Cognitive Services - consumed instead of built.
says: AI-as-a-Service is provided by public cloud providers as pre-trained generative AI models for your organization. The key offerings: Amazon AWS AI services, IBM Watson AI services, and Azure Cognitive Services.
explained: The value proposition is speed-to-capability. Vision, speech, language understanding, and now generative models take years and millions to build in-house; as a service they are an API key away (immediately usable, just by signing up for access). For most business features - document extraction, translation, summarization - the service is the rational default.

The architect's questions come after the yes: What data leaves our boundary when we call it? What does per-call pricing do at our scale (the inference-economy question)? What happens to our feature if the provider deprecates the model? AIaaS is the right starting point for most capabilities - with an exit plan, which is where private hosting and open models from his Season 1 episodes come in.
takeaway: Default to provider AI services for speed, but architect every call with the data-boundary, cost-at-scale, and exit questions answered.
